title: The Ugly Duckling
blurb: A duckling grows up wrong. He was never a duck at all.
script:
[warmly] Long, long ago… on a summer farm where the wheat stood tall and the water lay still and green, a mother duck sat waiting on her nest.

[excited] One by one the eggs began to crack. Out came a duckling… and another… and another. Small, and yellow, and soft.

[curious] But one egg was bigger than the rest. And it did not crack at all.

[thoughtful] The mother duck waited. And waited. [short pause] And at last, the big egg opened.

[surprised] Out tumbled a bird who was not yellow, and not small, and not soft. He was grey. He was gangly. His feet were far too large, and his neck was far too long.

[sad] “Oh dear,” said the other ducks. “What an ugly duckling.”

And after that, nobody was kind to him.

[gently] The ducklings would not swim beside him. The hens pecked at him when he came near the barn. Even the girl who brought the feed would push him away with her foot.

[softly] He would stand at the edge of the water, watching the others play… and he could not understand what was wrong with him.

[worried] So one evening, when the sky was going orange, the ugly duckling squeezed through a gap in the fence and walked away from the farm.

[softly] He walked through the reeds. He walked past the marsh. He slept under a bush and woke with frost on his back.

[sad] And everywhere he went, the wild birds looked at him and said the same thing. [whispers] “What ARE you?”

[slowly] The days grew short. The wind turned cold. The pond began to freeze at the edges, and the duckling pressed himself into the reeds to keep warm.

[sad] It was a long, hard, lonely winter. [short pause] And he was quite sure he would be alone forever.

[gently] But winter does not last. One morning he woke, and the ice was gone. The sun was warm on his back. Green things were pushing up through the mud.

[surprised] And down the river came three birds — the most beautiful birds he had ever seen. White as clouds. Necks curved like question marks. [softly] Swans.

[worried] “They will laugh at me too,” he thought. But he was so lonely that he swam towards them anyway.

[softly] And as he came close, he looked down into the still water… [short pause] and stopped.

[surprised] Because the bird looking back at him was not grey. Not gangly. Not ugly.

[warmly] He was white as a cloud. His neck curved like a question mark.

[gently] He had not been a bad duckling at all. He had been a young swan, the whole time — and nobody, not even he, had known it.
